analysis.investment_thesis: Capri Global Capital has delivered a genuinely remarkable 37.2% revenue CAGR and 30.4% earnings CAGR over nine years, building a diversified NBFC franchise (home loans, MSME, gold loans) serving India's massively underpenetrated credit markets — this is the kind of growth story I can respect. The constraint is that ROE of only 11.8% despite 2.52x leverage reveals significant capital inefficiency that must improve before I can endorse aggressive accumulation.
key_strengths: 37.2% revenue CAGR (FY16–FY25) with total assets growing from INR 4,441 Cr to INR 24,413 Cr in five years — compounding at exceptional speed in a large addressable market
Net profit grew 72% YoY (INR 279 Cr to INR 479 Cr, FY24–FY25) and 30.4% CAGR over nine years — earnings growth is accelerating, not slowing
Forward P/E of 12.96x provides a reasonable entry point for a business with this growth trajectory; the market appears to be under-pricing the earnings acceleration
key_risks: D/E of 2.52x with total debt rising from INR 4,832 Cr (FY22) to INR 15,577 Cr (FY25) — finance costs growing at 67.9% CAGR, faster than revenue, compresses net interest margins
ROE of 11.8% on 2.52x leverage is sub-optimal — a well-run NBFC with this gearing should deliver 18–22% ROE; the gap signals execution or credit-quality pressure
MSME and construction finance portfolios carry elevated NPA risk, especially in economic downturns; the loan book is less than a full credit cycle old at this scale
red_flags: OCF negative all 5 of 5 years (INR -4,312 Cr in FY25), reflecting aggressive loan disbursement — while normal for NBFCs, the scale of cash consumption requires continuous capital market access
Finance cost CAGR of 67.9% over nine years dwarfs revenue CAGR of 37.2% — the company is borrowing faster than it is earning, a pattern that can destabilize if funding markets tighten
Equity base nearly tripled between FY22 and FY23 (INR 1,922 Cr to INR 3,565 Cr) suggesting a large dilutive raise — existing shareholders bore significant dilution to fund growth
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Among these five stocks, Capri Global comes closest to my growth criteria — 37% revenue and 30% earnings CAGR sustained for nine years is genuinely exceptional and reflects management's ability to build distribution, access capital, and maintain credit discipline across multiple product lines (home loans, MSME, gold loans). India's MSME credit gap is estimated at INR 20-25 lakh crore, and Capri is addressing it with a scalable, technology-enabled model — a long runway exists.

However, the ROE-leverage mismatch troubles me deeply. At 2.52x D/E, a well-run NBFC should earn 18–22% ROE; earning only 11.8% means the risk-adjusted returns on the growing book are mediocre. The massive equity dilution of FY23 and the accelerating finance cost trajectory (67.9% CAGR) are warning signs that capital efficiency has not kept pace with book growth. I would want to see ROE trend meaningfully above 15% in the next 2 years before upgrading this to a strong buy — the growth story is real, but the capital economics must improve to justify concentrated ownership.
